author: Marshall
note: List of plates; no bearing on location.

author: Marshall
asr_identification: Taxila: Dharmarājikā (Chir Tope) stupa, Rawalpindi district
evidence: silver scroll (year 136 of Azes) in a gold casket buried under the Bodhisattva chapel G5 records relics enshrined "at the Dharmarājikā Stūpa in the Tanuva district of Takṣaśilā"; stratified chapels and Gandhāra sculpture dated 2nd c. AD
quote: At the Hharmarajika (Plate XIII), by which name I shall in future designate the “ Chir Tope,” … were enshrmed in the Bodhisattva chapel at the Hliarmarajika Slftpa in the Tannva •disti’ict of Taksha4ila
note: Inscription names Takṣaśilā on the site: confirms Taxila (Mizutani, agreed; the survey: Cunningham, ruins E of Shah-dheri). The Dharmarājikā is not itself a Xiyu ji place.

author: Marshall
note: Sirkap palace and Jandial temple; no Xiyu ji location argued.

author: Spooner (reported by Marshall)
asr_identification: Kumrahar site, Patna: palace of Pāṭaliputra (Mauryan "hall of columns")
evidence: excavated pillared hall at Kumrahar with columns 10 cubits apart; mounds on the site compared with the Persepolis platform; Mauryan level c. 20 ft below surface
quote: Dr. Spooner finds the likeness of the two so striking, that he is inclined to believe that the palace of Pataliputra was a direct replica of’ that of Persepolis, and that the small rocky hiU with a terrace and cave, which Hiuen Tsaug tells us once existed south-west of the old palace, was artificially constructed by the Mauryau emperor Asolca
note: Puts the Maurya palace, and Xuanzang's rock hill (Mahendra's cave) SW of it, at Kumrahar, SE of Bankipore; Mizutani places the city ruins between Patna and Dinapore (NW of Patna); the survey (Cunningham) had Mahendra's rock-house at Bara Pahari (Panch Pahari). Marshall stresses the conjecture is tentative.

author: Marshall (epigraphy summary)
asr_identification: country of the Malepadu plates of Punyakumāra (Cuddapah district)
evidence: Malepadu copper plates (c. 8th c.) of Cōḷa-Mahārājas subordinate to the Pallavas
quote: The jdates come from a part of the country which in the time of the Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang was called Chuliye ; and it is inferred that Punyakumara and others, who were of Ohola descent and hold the title Chola-Maharaja, must have been rulei’s of Chuliye under Pallaya overlords
note: Telugu-Cōḷa plates from the Cuddapah area taken as Xuanzang's Chuliye; differs from Mizutani (capital at Nellore); Venkayya's inland Kurnool/Cuddapah country — (Penner basin around Nellore). No survey entry.

author: Marshall
asr_identification: stupa on a plateau on the N side of the Hathial ridge, Taxila (with monastery)
evidence: excavated: rectangular three-tiered base 63 x 105 ft with N stair, semi-ashlar limestone, Corinthian pilasters; present stupa c. 3rd c. AD enclosing an earlier c. 1st-c. AD stupa 10 ft high; monastery beside it
quote: a stupa of imposing dimensions which occupies a commanding position on a plateau on the northern side of the Hatial ridge. This is the stupa which Hiuen Tsang describes as hemg more than 100 feet high and which he says was erected to commemorate the spot where Asoka’s son Kunala had his eyes put out
note: Marshall's identification, followed by Mizutani (N slope of the Hathial ridge S of Sirkap). Moves the survey's Kunāla stupa (Cunningham: Kurmal tope SE of the Bir mound).

author: Marshall
note: Besnagar; Sarnath digs by Hargreaves (Gupta images) without location argument; Kāmarūpa (Nidhanpur plates) history only.

author: Marshall
name_in_asr: stupa of the ‘Sacrificed Head’; Bhalar Stupa
evidence: drum underpinned and refaced; square terrace and adjoining monastery (reputed seat of Kumāralabdha) still to be cleared
quote: The conservation of the Bhalar Stupa, which I have now been able to identify with the stupa of the ‘ Sacrificed Head ’ described by Hiuen Thsang
note: New identification by Marshall, the one Mizutani follows (Bhallar stupa, W end of Sarda hill). Moves the survey's site (Cunningham: Babar Khana N of the city). The monastery is tied to Kumāralabdha, whom Xuanzang places in Taxila.

author: Marshall; Spooner
asr_identification: Sirsukh city walls (Taxila); Bara Pahari mound (Patna); Nālandā (Bargaon)
evidence: Sirsukh: SE corner of fortifications cleared, Kushan large-diaper masonry with round loopholed bastions; 3rd-4th c. block in the city centre. Bara Pahari: trial digging found two Mauryan stupas on a lofty platform. Nālandā: first trial trenches; monastery wall over 200 ft; inscribed seals
quote: In the city of Sirsukh itself I cleared a section of the fortifications at the south-east corner of the city, and found that they were constructed of the large diaper masonry characteristic of the Kushan epoch … trial excavations were commenced at Bara Pahari, where the great Asokan stupas are supposed to lie, and this resulted in the location of two structures of this type, which seem to beof Mauryan date
note: Kushan walls of Sirsukh support Mizutani's capital of Xuanzang's day (Sirsukh, not Bhir Mound or Sirkap; the survey: Cunningham's Bir mound). The Mauryan stupas at Bara Pahari bear on Cunningham's Asoka stupas at Panch Pahari (ASR 11); Mizutani gives no site for the 84,000 stupa. Nālandā only begun here.

author: Marshall
note: Taxila: Dharmarajika and Sirkap N gate; no Xiyu ji location argued.

author: Spooner
evidence: Site 1 rebuilt at least four times; finds include multiple official seals of the Nālandā establishment, a Gupta official seal, bronze pillar
quote: The finds at Site No. 1 include multiple examples of the official seal of the Nalanda establishment, which for some as yet unknown reason shows the same insignia as that of the establishment at Sarnath
note: Seals name the monastery on the site: confirms Bargaon = Nālandā (Mizutani, agreed; the survey: Cunningham, Baragaon).

author: Spooner (epigraphy summary)
evidence: many clay seals of one type reading Śrī-Nālandā-mahāvihārīy-ārya-bhikṣu-saṅghasya with wheel and two deer; Gupta seal of Nagarabhukti
quote: a large find of inseribed terracotta plaques and clay seals in the excavations at Nalanda. Twen of these are of one type and bear the legend Sri-Nalanda-Mahavihariy-Arya-Bhikshu-Sanghasya
note: The strongest evidence: seals of the "great vihāra of Śrī-Nālandā" on the site; confirms Mizutani and Cunningham.

author: Spooner
note: Conservation (Purana Qila; Sarnath clearance; Kunala monastery repairs).

author: Spooner (DG report)
asr_identification: Early Cōḷa country (Cuddapah district); Nālandā N of Rajgir
evidence: inscriptions of Chola-Mahārāja and Mangi-Chola (c. 9th c.); Nālandā Site 1 shows a fifth, older monastery; long N-S trench through the western stupa row
quote: to whose country the Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsiang gave the name Chuliye … the famous monasteries and stupas at Nalanda, north of Rajgir in the Patna District of Bihar, was continued
note: Chuliye again tied to the Early Cōḷas of Cuddapah (differs from Mizutani (capital at Nellore); Venkayya's inland Kurnool/Cuddapah country —'s Penner basin). Nālandā: no new locating evidence.

author: Sahni
evidence: excavation round the pillar, which was re-erected; pillar uninscribed with Asokan polish; the Allahabad pillar's edict to the rulers of Kauśāmbī taken as brought from here; 7th-c. inscription shows it still standing then
quote: The fact that Yuan Chwang makes no mention of any Asoka pillars in his account of Kian-shang-mi, or Kau.'fitmbl, offers no serious difficulty … one of the inscriptions on it is definitely addressed by the Emperor Asoka to the rulers of Kausambl
note: Assumes Kosam = Kauśāmbī (Mizutani and Cunningham agree) and explains Xuanzang's silence on the pillar.

author: Hargreaves
asr_identification: Shahbazgarhi village, 9 miles ENE of Mardan (Peshawar district); Mekha-Sanda hill NE of the village

quote: the excavated site at Ba.sarh in the Muzaffarpur District, whicli lias been identified with the ancient Vaisaii. the capital of the Lichchavis … Excavations carried out by Dr. Bloch in lf)03 went far to establish proof of the correctness of this identilication … has been identified with tliat described by the 7th ceutury D. Chinese pilgrim Yiian Chwang as marking the place wliere the Buddha liad appeared

author: Sahni
asr_identification: Thanesar: old fort, Bahari fort and town mounds (Karnal district); stupa mound ¾ mile NW of Thanesar
evidence: three mounds together c. 3 miles round; fort bricks 14 x 10 x 2½ in., dated to c. 7th c. (Harṣa); a W gate of the fort located, rampart 11 ft thick; excavation at Raja Karn ka Qila nearby

author: Sahni
evidence: excavation at site F: pair of torana pillars and the Kumāragupta pillars (AD 415-16); Maitreya image with the Buddhist creed; late-Gupta Śaiva images; Cunningham's 35-ft mound with large Mauryan-size bricks not yet bottomed
quote: General Cunningham, who inspected this place twice,* identifies it with the … Pi-h-shan-na uientioiied by Yiian Chwang, and this identification appears to be unquestiona})le
note: Agrees with Mizutani (Bilsar) and with Cunningham's later view (ASR XI); the Aśoka stupa and two monasteries still unlocated.

note: Frontier: Zar Dheri, Kot, Khalo near Hund, Ishpola; no Xiyu ji identification.

author: Spooner (DG report)
note: Frontier explorations near Jamalgarhi; no Xiyu ji identification.

author: Page; Dikshit
evidence: Nālandā: nine levels in monastery 1 (c. 6th-12th c.); site 4 monastery cleared; Dikshit traces old embanked roads in Varendra towards Mahāsthān
quote: in the area now designated site N<». 4 (according to (General Cunningham, the monastery of the Buddha (lupta of Yuan (^hwang's accountf) … connecting the city of Paundravardhana (probably Mahasthana) with ancient localities
note: Nālandā: Cunningham's attribution of site 4 to Buddhagupta's monastery (ASR I) reported, not tested. Puṇḍravardhana = Mahāsthān only "probably" (as Mizutani).

author: Page
asr_identification: Rummindei (Nepal Tarai); Kushinagara said to be in the same territory
quote: from the birth in the Lumbini Grove at Rummindei, in the modern Nepalese Terai, to the Nirvana at Kushinagara in the same territory
note: Museum note describing a stele. Lumbinī = Rummindei as Mizutani; putting Kuśinagara in the Nepal Tarai is a passing remark (against Kasia, Mizutani's and Cunningham's site), with no evidence.

author: Spooner (DG report)
note: Chemist; Mathura art (Pāvā = Padrauna mentioned, not a Xiyu ji place).

author: Page
asr_identification: Sobnath Hill beside Hasia (Hasra) Kol, Gaya district
quote: of the early Buddhist sites at Hasia Kol and the Sobnath Hill adjacent, vrhich latter has been identified with the Kakkutapada Hill of the Chinese pilgrims where Kasyapa the contemporary disciple of Buddha lies buried
note: Differs from Mizutani (hill 1 mile N of Kurkihar) and from Cunningham (hills N of Kurkihar / Murali hill); the identifier is not named.
